title: Modifier Key Framework rule file
description: One file per mod in Data/SKSE/Plugins/ModifierKeyFramework/*.json. Comments (// and /* */) are allowed.

version.description: Rule format version this file is written for. Files without it are version 1. Version 2 (framework 1.1.0): primary and its label are optional. Version 3 (framework 1.2.0): alternate can be a list of up to 3 actions. Version 4 (framework 1.3.0): the topic condition, and actions that pick a dialogue topic (topic, endDialogue). Version 5 (framework 1.4.0): object targets and do actions.

translations.description: Name of the translation file for $Key labels: Interface/Translations/<name>_<LANGUAGE>.txt. Default: this file's name without .json.

id.description: Name of the rule: shown in the log, sent with the event, used by SetRuleEnabled.

target.description: What the rule applies to: NPCs, or (version 5) objects in the world (books, items, doors, containers), which use the object conditions.

not.description: Conditions of which none may hold.

primary.description: The action when activating normally. Without a label the prompt keeps the game's own text (e.g. Search). Optional (version 2).

alternate.description: The action while the modifier key is held (Activate), or (version 3) a list of up to 3 in order of importance: buttons Activate, X, Y. Adds the modifier key's button (or the marker, default '+') to the primary label. Each needs a label. A topic action shows only while the NPC offers one of its topics; the ones after it move up a button.

priority.description: When several rules match, the highest wins; ties go to the file name that sorts first.

enabled.description: false: off until a script calls ModifierKeyFramework.SetRuleEnabled(file, id, true).

label.description: Text on the first prompt line, or a $Key from the translation file.

event.description: SKSE mod event sent on activation: Event(String eventName, String ruleId, Float afAction, Form target). Without it (and without a topic), only the label changes and activation stays vanilla.

topic.description: Version 4, instead of an event: start the conversation and pick the first listed dialogue topic (DIAL) the NPC offers, as if the player had chosen it: the NPC turns to the player, says the line and does what it does (open the barter menu, ...).

do.description: Version 5, instead of an event: one of the game's own actions. activate = the vanilla activation; take = pick it up (a crime where the game says so); equip / equipAndDraw = pick up and equip (and draw); use = pick up and drink / eat / apply. Without a label, activate and take show the game's own word. NPC rules can only activate.

info.description: Version 5: what the prompt's last line shows while this is the action on Activate, instead of the game's (a lock level, ...). relationship = how the NPC, the people living behind a door, or an object's owner feel about the player.

infoLabels.description: With info relationship: the rule's own words per rank range instead of the game's rank names. The first entry whose fromRank the rank reaches is shown (4 Lover ... 1 Friend, 0 Acquaintance ... -4 Archnemesis); an entry without fromRank covers every rank.

label.description: Plain text, or a $Key from the rule file's translation file.

endDialogue.description: Version 4, with topic: close the conversation when the menu the topic opened (barter, training, gift, ...) closes.

forms.description: One form, or a list: any one of them counts.

keyword.description: Has the keyword (on the NPC or its race).

faction.description: Is in the faction (optionally with a minimum rank). A list: any one of them.

npc.description: Is this NPC (base NPC record, not a placed reference).

topic.description: Version 4: offers one of these dialogue topics (DIAL) right now: the topic's quest runs and one of its lines passes its conditions (e.g. a merchant whose shop is open).

type.description: Object rules (version 5): the object is one of these kinds.

base.description: Object rules (version 5): is one of these base objects.

read.description: Object rules (version 5): is a book the player has read.

spellTome.description: Object rules (version 5): is a spell tome.

takeable.description: Object rules (version 5): can be picked up.

owned.description: Object rules (version 5): taking it is a crime.

requiresKey.description: Object rules (version 5): is locked and only its key opens it.

playerHasKey.description: Object rules (version 5): is locked and the player carries its key.

destinationKeyword.description: Object rules (version 5): a door whose other side is in a location with this keyword.

interior.description: Version 5: the target is in an interior cell.
